1.web: Immediately in the morning the chief priests, with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
1.asv: And straightway in the morning the chief priests with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.

2.web: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered, “So you say.”
2.asv: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering saith unto him, Thou sayest.

3.web: The chief priests accused him of many things.
3.asv: And the chief priests accused him of many things.

4.web: Pilate again asked him, “Have you no answer? See how many things they testify against you!”
4.asv: And Pilate again asked him, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they accuse thee of.

5.web: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.
5.asv: But Jesus no more answered anything; insomuch that Pilate marvelled.

6.web: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.
6.asv: Now at the feast he used to release unto them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.

7.web: There was one called Barabbas, bound with those who had made insurrection, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
7.asv: And there was one called Barabbas, lying bound with them that had made insurrection, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.

8.web: The multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for them.
8.asv: And the multitude went up and began to ask him to do as he was wont to do unto them.

9.web: Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
9.asv: And Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

10.web: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
10.asv: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.

11.web: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
11.asv: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.

12.web: Pilate again asked them, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”
12.asv: And Pilate again answered and said unto them, What then shall I do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?

13.asv: And they cried out again, Crucify him.

14.web: Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”
14.asv: And Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out exceedingly, Crucify him.

15.web: Pilate, wishing to please the multitude, released Barabbas to them, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.
15.asv: And Pilate, wishing to content the multitude, released unto them Barabbas, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

16.web: The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.
16.asv: And the soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Prætorium; and they call together the whole band.

17.web: They clothed him with purple, and weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on him.
17.asv: And they clothe him with purple, and platting a crown of thorns, they put it on him;

18.web: They began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
18.asv: and they began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!

19.web: They struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and bowing their knees, did homage to him.
19.asv: And they smote his head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.

20.web: When they had mocked him, they took the purple off of him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
20.asv: And when they had mocked him, they took off from him the purple, and put on him his garments. And they lead him out to crucify him.

21.web: They compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.
21.asv: And they compel one passing by, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.

22.web: They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”
22.asv: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.

23.web: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.
23.asv: And they offered him wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.

24.web: Crucifying him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots on them, what each should take.
24.asv: And they crucify him, and part his garments among them, casting lots upon them, what each should take.

25.web: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
25.asv: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

26.web: The superscription of his accusation was written over him, “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
26.asv: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

27.web: With him they crucified two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
27.asv: And with him they crucify two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.

28.web: The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, “He was numbered with transgressors.”

29.web: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days,
29.asv: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ha! thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,

30.web: save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
30.asv: save thyself, and come down from the cross.

31.web: Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes said, “He saved others. He can’t save himself.
31.asv: In like manner also the chief priests mocking him among themselves with the scribes said, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

32.web: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.” Those who were crucified with him insulted him.
32.asv: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reproached him.

33.web: When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
33.asv: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.

34.web: At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
34.asv: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

35.web: Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”
35.asv: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elijah.

36.web: One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
36.asv: And one ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let be; let us see whether Elijah cometh to take him down.

37.web: Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and gave up the spirit.
37.asv: And Jesus uttered a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.

38.web: The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
38.asv: And the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom.

39.web: When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
39.asv: And when the centurion, who stood by over against him, saw that he so gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.

40.web: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
40.asv: And there were also women beholding from afar: among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;

41.web: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and served him; and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.
41.asv: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him; and many other women that came up with him unto Jerusalem.

42.web: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
42.asv: And when even was now come, because it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

43.web: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for the Kingdom of God, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
43.asv: there came Joseph of Arimathæa, a councillor of honorable estate, who also himself was looking for the kingdom of God; and he boldly went in unto Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.

44.web: Pilate marveled if he were already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.
44.asv: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

45.web: When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
45.asv: And when he learned it of the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

46.web: He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
46.asv: And he bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been hewn out of a rock; and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

47.web: Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
47.asv: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.
